machine.shared: A development machine, at rest for this study: every round ran under the lock of the measurements; the two agents of the machine, a logcenter and three gates of an application stayed up, idle.

build.tls: OpenSSL 3.6.5 (bundled, static: linux-ext-libs 1.28); mbedTLS not built on this machine
build.note: CONFIG_DEBUG_TRACK_MEMORY is on (the .config of this machine): every allocation is tracked. A build without it does less work per allocation; that build was not measured here.

method.ab: Written on 2026-11-13, before the tag. 7.31.1 is the C code of main at 3c53c9075, measured against 7.31.0, the last release with a study. Its only C change is llhttp 9.4.4 (the vendored llhttp.c of gobj-c): of the objects of the SDK only llhttp.c.o has other machine code, and the stripped binaries keep the size of 7.31.0. Both sides are git worktrees (yunetas-perf-7.31.0 and yunetas-perf-7.31.1) built by `yunetas init --sdk-only` and `make install` of the kernel libraries and modules into their own outputs/, the benchmarks and the three ctest binaries from their root build/; outputs_ext is a copy of the main tree's (linux-ext-libs 1.28 on both sides). the binaries pinned to one CPU (taskset -c 6) and run in rotation, the order turned each round, a sync and a 3 s pause (1 s for the three ctest binaries) before each run: 10 rounds. Mean +- standard deviation (median), t = the change over its standard error; |t| < 3 is noise. The two figures outside their noise (both faster) and the two request parsers were measured again, 10 more rounds of their two benchmarks (perf_c_treedb, perf_micro); their reasons give both runs. The BFF figure and the event loop echoes are means of the samples of a run, the first left out (and the last, for the echoes). The treedb figures (perf_tr_treedb, perf_tr_treedb_read) are CPU time of the process; perf_c_treedb is wall time. The page-by-page read rate is the mean of the FORWARD and BACKWARD passes of test_topic_pkey_integer_iterator5. perf_http and perf_micro are the drivers written for the 7.31.0 study, kept since. No hardware counters (perf_event_paranoid is 4 on this machine and no root). The rounds ran with the machine at rest, a load average of 0.7 to 2.
method.tag_run: The absolute figures of 7.31.1 are its side of the A/B run (main at 3c53c9075), measured on 2026-11-13. The commit of the release after it changes no .c file. The binary sizes are those of the yunos of that worktree, built with the same .config (make, not installed).

story.title: Yuneta 7.31.1 against 7.31.0
story.lead: 7.31.1 takes llhttp 9.4.4, the HTTP parser every yuno that speaks HTTP runs: a header value with a byte only the lenient mode accepts goes back to the fast scanner. It is the only C change. Measured against 7.31.0 before the tag: all 66 figures inside their noise, and the binaries keep their size.

hero.text: figures inside their noise against 7.31.0: one object changed (llhttp.c.o), and the request parsers measured about 1% faster in two runs, too little to claim.

tiles: Parse a request that arrives in pieces
Records read per second, page by page
treedb: update a node in memory
story.ab_sub: Each benchmark built from the tree of each release (7.31.0 and 7.31.1), pinned to one CPU, the binaries run in rotation: 10 rounds. A change inside its whisker is noise.
story.prices_sub: What got slower, how much, and what it buys. These are the only figures slower because of a change.
story.abs_sub: Absolute figures of the 7.31.1 build (main at 3c53c9075), measured on 2026-11-13 on the laptop above, as its side of the A/B run: one process, pinned to one CPU. Mean of the 10 rounds.
story.no_prices: No figure is slower outside its noise: there is no price to name in this release.
